What is Gemini Notebook (NotebookLM)?

Google’s source-based research and note-taking tool brings uploaded documents and discovered sources into a notebook. It supports cited answers, summaries and other formats for exploring a collection of material.

Best for

Answering questions from a closed, trusted set of your own documents.

Main features

  • Add documents and other supported sources to a notebook
  • Ask questions with citations to notebook material
  • Discover sources from the web or Google Drive
  • Use research workflows to gather additional sources
  • Create summaries and audio overviews of notebook material

Practical use cases

  • Studying from lecture notes and textbooks
  • synthesising a set of client documents
  • producing a briefing from 20 reports
  • generating an audio summary of dense material for a commute
  • onboarding on a new codebase or policy set.

Who is it for?

  • Students, researchers, analysts, consultants, legal and compliance teams, anyone synthesising a defined document set.

Pricing, free access & limits

Free with paid limits raised through the Google AI subscription ladder

Plans described in the source

Free with generous limits (typically 100 notebooks, 50 sources each). NotebookLM Pro capabilities are bundled into Google AI Pro at $19.99/mo and Google AI Ultra at $99.99/$199.99, raising notebook and source limits roughly 5x and adding higher Audio Overview quotas. Also available through Google Workspace with admin controls.

Free plan

Yes - substantial free tier that covers most individual use.

Free trial

Google AI Pro trials appear periodically; the free NotebookLM tier is the practical trial.

Usage limits to consider

Free tier caps notebooks, sources per notebook, daily chat queries and Audio Overview generations. Paid tiers multiply these roughly 5x. Individual source size limits apply (word/page count per document).

Strengths & tradeoffs

These points summarize the supplied research, rather than hands-on test results.

Strengths noted in the source

  • Source citations help readers trace answers to the underlying material
  • Multiple output formats support different ways of exploring documents
  • Web source discovery can expand the material in a notebook

Limitations to consider

  • Answers still need to be checked against the original sources
  • Source counts, file sizes and usage limits depend on the plan
  • Check account-specific data policies before using confidential material

Platforms, languages & integrations

Platforms

  • Web, iOS, Android

Languages

  • Supports 35+ languages for output; Audio Overviews available in a growing set including Arabic and French

API access

Limited public API; Workspace admin APIs for enterprise deployment

Integrations and exports

  • Google Drive, Docs, Slides, YouTube, PDF/URL/text upload, Google Workspace

Evaluation notes

The workbook’s claim that this tool cannot search the web was corrected using Google’s source-discovery documentation. Source grounding should not be treated as a guarantee of accuracy or suitability for regulated data.
